content.text: All preferred elements are present in § 22, and § 23 imposes no parallel audit obligation.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: § 22 satisfies the preferred position in full: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period (22.1), require at least thirty days' prior written notice (22.1), occur during normal business hours (22.1), are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent (22.2), and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly (22.2). § 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains no operative text and imposes no parallel audit or inspection obligation on us, and no other audit/verification right binding Customer appears in the document. The additional protections in 22.2–22.3 (no access to unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or third-party confidential information; findings treated as our Confidential Information; shortfall payment resolving the issue) run in our favour and are not flagged. No redline required.
